title: Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com)
summary: He picks apart a Natty or Not article claiming light weights beat heavy ones and that naturals hit hard strength limits. He defends strength work as key to bodybuilding, says joint pain is avoidable with good programming, and rejects the blackpill mindset of settling for good enough.
claims: Letting an old man's comment keep you out of the gym for a month shows a weak mind; do not take advice from people who believe in a natural limit
He could not go two days without lifting
Pain that persists after switching to good form may simply be an existing injury; he broke ribs and the pain remained even deadlifting with perfect form
Believing the world is against you no matter what you do is a victim's mentality
You can get stronger without gaining weight: he has stayed around or below 210 lb while all his lifts went up, without injury or joint pain
If a weight drains you, stay at it and progress; if the same weight, reps and tonnage still drain you after two months, you need more stimulus from close variations or your recovery is bad
Joint pain is easy to avoid with five things: good nutrition, low stress, good sleep, good technique and good volume and intensity manipulation
He used to have constant elbow, biceps tendon, knee, lower back and neck pain until he learned to program instead of doing compounds and variations with no control
Squat, bench and deadlift do not cover every movement pattern; a real base covers them all, and a base is meant to be built upon: the higher the tower, the wider the base
Strength work is not only for strength athletes; it is key for bodybuilding
He builds his physique for himself and wants to inspire people, not humiliate them
Naturals mostly cannot compete with PED users because PEDs work; he bears no ill will toward users and would encourage them to try a period clean
Functional training is contextual and mostly nonsense; bodybuilders train to get bigger and need not justify it
Getting stronger on the squat strengthens every knee flexion variation and raises tonnage, so you grow: his legs went from 26 to 26.5 inches as all his leg lifts got stronger
Adding 50 lb to your bench makes you look like a different person; 50 lb on the deadlift still brings some growth
Adding 50 lb to a lift takes great sacrifice and time, and that is simply life, not a reason to quit
The neurological adaptation from learning a new lift is gone after about six months of weekly practice; after that strength gains are muscle
Small increases in muscle size produce surprisingly large increases in strength
Joints strengthen far too slowly to explain yearly strength gains, and muscles do not just get denser without growing
You need weight progression on the bar; without it your physique eventually stops progressing
Three years of training is not advanced; at three years he was 170 lb; advanced means a decade of hard training, so he calls himself intermediate with some advanced body parts
You get stronger by doing reps and mixing rep ranges
Using straps, a mixed grip or hook grip on deadlifts is not cheating; only lifting what you can grip is a stupid idea
The zen mindset does not mean becoming a stone; keep evolving, because stagnancy is death
People who want the moon and work like maniacs are happy; those who talk but avoid hard work are miserable
The spirit matters more than the body; his transformation came from his mind
Good enough is mediocre; his channel is about continually pushing to be exceptional
The only gains that last a lifetime are natural ones
